Public data only. Voices are AI-generated; all content is editorially produced.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 20, 2026
item.description: WTI October settled $99.53 (-2.3%) and Brent November $103.19 (-1.6%) on Friday, while the Canadian diff complex heads into the week with no fresh public prints.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 21, 2026
item.description: Keystone ran at 94% of available capacity, rail's share of exports rose to 7.1% in June, and the WTI October contract expires Tuesday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 22, 2026
item.description: Yanbu exports could resume today, Brent fell $2+ to its lowest since Sep 8, and the WTI October contract expired after a four-session slide of roughly $10.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 23, 2026
item.description: "Reconstructed edition — the morning run failed; rebuilt from the day's wires and the following edition. WTI and Brent closed Tuesday at two-week lows after six straight down days; the Saudi East-West restart was confirmed; EIA weekly due Wednesday morning."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 24, 2026
item.description: "Flat price rallied 3–4% Wednesday on a diesel-export-ban headline the White House then denied, plus fresh Hormuz attacks. The EIA's bearish 3-million-barrel build was shrugged off. Joliet still dark; diesel cracks over $100 keep synthetic crude bid."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 25, 2026
item.description: "Brent and WTI giving back Thursday's Houthi-missile rally on overnight US–Iran truce signals. Several Joliet units returned Wednesday — the front-of-strip WCS catalyst. Diesel cracks re-testing records; October Merey sales stalled on record freight."

item.title: Heavy Reading morning digest — September 26, 2026
item.description: "Trump rejected Iran's 7-day truce offer after the Friday settle — Hormuz re-closed, ships attacked off Oman, Houthis took Perim Island. Friday's crude selloff is at risk of full reversal on Sunday reopen. Joliet only partially restarting; gasoil cracks printed a record."

item.title: Heavy Reading morning digest — September 27, 2026
item.description: "Trump publicly rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz plan Saturday — Friday's crude selloff may not survive the Sunday reopen. But Gulf tanker volumes have doubled in a month, so the premium is doing more work than the flows. Joliet still only partially back; WTI specs sit at the 96th percentile of length."

item.title: Heavy Reading morning digest — September 28, 2026
item.description: "A ~275 kb/d Midwest (PADD 2) heavy-crude buyer is back online. Meanwhile Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap, and Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries hit its biggest weekend of 2026."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 29, 2026
item.description: Joliet's restart awaits public confirmation, Whiting union talks reconvene today, and crude firms as Hormuz diplomacy stalls.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 30, 2026
item.description: First ICE settlements in days show the WCS front widening $1.40 while both PADD 2 demand binaries break bearish; the Moscow refinery is halted overnight and US tanker enforcement goes transoceanic.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 1, 2026
item.description: Gulf crude flows are back near pre-war levels and Brent fell to ~$96 in Asia before recovering; the product market is in full distress with record cracks. TMW Nov26 tightened 50c to -$21.60 while December sits widest at -$22.40, staring at the 40-million-barrel SPR exchange.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 2, 2026
item.description: Brent settled $102.31 after WSJ reported a third carrier strike group and up to 10,000 troops heading to the Gulf; TMW Nov26 settled -$23.75 (ICE, Oct 1) while WTI rallied, the prompt pricing a November-December egress crunch. Diesel crack $101.74, eighteen straight closes above $100. Pacific Link designated Canada's first project of national interest.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 5, 2026
item.description: OPEC+ held November targets steady on Sunday and crude faded on the overnight tape (WTI ~$89.69, Brent ~$101.67) while heating oil rose 1.4%, pushing the diesel crack back above $100 on the session print. ING marked the ICE gasoil crack $85 to $70. TMW Nov26 held -$24.13 (ICE, Oct 2) with December at -$24.65 the widest tenor; Joliet is confirmed back in service; the SPR exchange bids are due Tuesday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 6, 2026
item.description: WTI hovered near $89.33 overnight while Brent held around $100.28; Saudi Aramco cut its Arab Light official price for Asia to a six-year low as Middle East exports beat pre-war levels four days last week. The diesel crack settled back above $100 Monday ($101.47). Today's binary: SPR exchange bids due 11:00 a.m. Central.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 7, 2026
item.description: Brent December traded around $101.6 overnight (+1%) and WTI around $90.2 (+0.9%) after Saudi Arabia confirmed Houthi strikes on Jazan and Najran airports and a Gulf of Mexico storm formed over offshore production. Tuesday's session had Brent trading down to a $97.06 intraday low before recovering to settle $100.58 (+$0.26); WTI settled $89.44 (DTN). The diesel crack settled $102.47 Tuesday; SPR exchange bids went in with no award announced yet.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 8, 2026
item.description: Hurricane Isaias (75 mph, possibly Cat 3) tracks toward a Mobile landfall early Oct 10 with ~511 kb/d of Gulf oil shut in; Houthi strikes killed three at Saudi airports and a tanker took projectiles north of Qatar. Wednesday's session was sold on the IEA agreeing to accelerate the strategic release and prioritize diesel: WTI settled $88.28 (-$1.16), Brent $100.20 (-$0.38); overnight Brent Dec ran back to ~$102.35 (+~2.2%). The diesel crack settled $105.87 Wednesday, its third straight close above $100. ICE (Oct 7): TMW Nov26 -$24.62, Dec26 -$25.15 still the widest tenor; ARV Nov26 -$15.69. EIA: crude drew 3.2 Mbbl vs +1.7 expected; Cushing built a third week.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 9, 2026
item.description: Hurricane Isaias strengthened to 90 kt overnight with a Mobile-area landfall early Oct 10; BSEE shut-ins more than doubled Thursday to 1,282,879 b/d (62.89%) with 121 platforms evacuated. Thursday's session was the storm bid: WTI ~+$3.21, Brent ~+$4.08; overnight the tape gave back ~$1 on track uncertainty. The diesel crack's overnight print runs ~$111.60 (provisional). ICE (Oct 8): TMW Nov26 -$24.69, Dec26 -$25.35 still the widest tenor; ARV Nov26 -$15.93. The SPR exchange award is still pending; CFTC positioning releases today.
